name: parse + first validation pass (total)
note: CI-calibrated, not the PRD's literal 2000ms (ADR-034): the first real CI run (v0.9.0 #1) measured mean 4086.22ms / max 4605.19ms on GitHub's shared ubuntu-latest runner, about 7x slower than the same benchmark on a normal dev machine (580.57ms). The PRD's 2-second target describes real end-user hardware, which this CI job cannot represent for this specific CPU-bound workload — 7000ms (~1.5x the observed CI max) catches real regressions without false-failing on ordinary CI noise.

name: single moveSeqItem
note: PRD's literal figure, unadjusted: CI measured ~0.01ms, about four orders of magnitude of margin, so CI/real-hardware differences cannot plausibly close this gap.

name: 100 consecutive moves
note: PRD's literal figure, unadjusted: CI measured ~1.95ms, about 50x margin.

name: applyBatch-equivalent replacing 1000 rule targets
note: CI-calibrated, not the PRD's literal 100ms (ADR-034): CI measured ~78.25ms, only ~1.28x margin — too tight for a brand-new gate on a noisy shared runner. 150ms keeps a real 2x+ slowdown catchable while giving headroom against normal CI jitter; tighten once more real CI runs are on record.
